claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model-card release is compliant and evidentially supported despite a current emergency-shelter-placement subgroup weakness below warning threshold.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use suspicious when aggregate evidence points toward launch readiness but a required support link remains unresolved.
Do not treat prior approvals or informal monitoring as substitutes for current release evidence under the stated policy.
Public governance guidance can support general documentation practice, but it cannot cure a missing internal policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the current model-card or release documentation showing the shelter-placement weakness is explicitly disclosed.
Provide approved mitigation or risk-acceptance records covering launch with this named use-case weakness.
Provide the materiality determination, if any, explaining why this subgroup weakness would not require disclosure under policy.
Provide the current evaluation artifact for the affected segment and any linked launch decision record referencing it.
specific_concerns: The actor summary itself says the shelter-placement subgroup is 1.5 percentage points below the warning threshold in the current release.
Policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses unless covered by approved mitigation.
The admissible record, as summarized, does not include approved risk acceptance, reviewed mitigation, or attached disclosure language for the subgroup weakness.
Prior family approval is stale for this purpose because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
Informal post-launch monitoring comments are contextual only and do not satisfy the policy requirement for current evidence or reviewed mitigation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record without explicit current disclosure or approved mitigation for the subgroup weakness.
That prior approval or informal monitoring can substitute for current release evidence and reviewed risk acceptance.
